# CLI reference

Every command and option of `limen`, generated from the binary. For examples and how the commands fit together, see [the CLI guide](guides/cli.md).

## `limen`

Limen command-line client.

```text
Usage: limen [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--color <WHEN>`: When to use colour: auto, always, or never. Values: auto, always, never. Default: `auto`.
- `--proxy <PROXY>`: Proxy address, for example `limen.example.com:443`. Defaults to the last one used. Environment: `LIMEN_PROXY`.
- `-d, --detach`: Run a `connect` command in the background and return once it is listening.

### `limen login`

Log in through the identity provider and get short-lived credentials

```text
Usage: limen login [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--device`: Use the device code flow, for machines without a browser.
- `--no-browser`: Print the login URL instead of opening a browser.
- `--ca-file <CA_FILE>`: CA certificate to trust for the proxy. Pinned for later commands.
- `--bot <METHOD>`: Log in as a bot with this CI platform's identity token, instead of as a person. In GitHub Actions the token is requested for you. Values: github_actions, gitlab, oidc.
- `--bot-name <NAME>`: Which bot, if more than one could match the token.
- `--token-env <VAR>`: Read the token from this environment variable (default for gitlab and oidc: LIMEN_ID_TOKEN).
- `--token-file <FILE>`: Read the token from this file, or `-` for standard input.
- `--audience <AUD>`: The audience to ask GitHub for. Defaults to the one the control plane expects.

### `limen logout`

Delete local credentials

```text
Usage: limen logout [OPTIONS]
```

### `limen status`

Show the current identity, roles, and when the credentials expire

```text
Usage: limen status [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--json`: Output JSON instead of text.

### `limen ls`

List resources you are allowed to access

```text
Usage: limen ls [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
```

Arguments:

- `<QUERY>`: Only resources whose name or a label contains this text (case-insensitive).

Options:

- `--json`: Output JSON instead of a table.
- `--watch <SECS>`: Redraw the list every SECS seconds (default 2) until interrupted.
- `-q, --quiet`: Print only the resource names, one per line, for scripts and shell loops.
- `--label <KEY=VALUE>`: Only resources with this label (`key=value`). Repeat to require several.
- `--type <KIND>`: Only resources of this type, such as `postgres` or `ssh`.

### `limen request`

Ask for access to a resource for a limited time, with a reason

```text
Usage: limen request [OPTIONS] <RESOURCE>
```

Arguments:

- `<RESOURCE>`

Options:

- `--role <ROLE>`: Which requestable role, when more than one reaches the resource.
- `--for <DURATION>`: How long you need it, such as 30m or 2h. The role sets the limit.
- `-m, --reason <REASON>`: Why. Approvers and auditors read it; some roles want a ticket id in it.
- `--break-glass`: Use a break-glass role: granted at once, and reviewed afterwards.
- `--wait`: Wait for an approver instead of returning.
- `--json`

### `limen requests`

Your access requests. `--approvals` shows the ones waiting for you

```text
Usage: limen requests [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--approvals`: Requests you may approve or deny.
- `--all`: Every request (limen:admin or limen:auditor).
- `--status <STATUS>`: pending, approved, denied, expired, cancelled, or revoked.
- `--json`

### `limen approve`

Approve an access request. Never your own

```text
Usage: limen approve [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`

Options:

- `-m, --comment <COMMENT>`

### `limen deny`

Deny an access request

```text
Usage: limen deny [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`

Options:

- `-m, --comment <COMMENT>`

### `limen cancel`

Withdraw an access request of yours that is still waiting

```text
Usage: limen cancel [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`

### `limen explain`

Say why you can or cannot reach a resource

```text
Usage: limen explain [OPTIONS] <RESOURCE>
```

Arguments:

- `<RESOURCE>`

Options:

- `--as <KIND=NAME>`: What you would use on it, such as login=ubuntu or db_role=limen_read.
- `--database <DATABASE>`: With db_role or mongo_role: the database.
- `--user <USER>`: Explain for this user, with the full trace (limen:admin).
- `--json`

### `limen review`

Access reviews waiting for you: `limen review ls`, `certify`, `flag`

```text
Usage: limen review [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `limen review start`

Start an access review: a snapshot of who holds which role, sent to its owners

```text
Usage: limen review start [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--name <NAME>`
- `--due-days <DUE_DAYS>`: Days the reviewers have (default 14). Default: `14`.
- `--override-days <OVERRIDE_DAYS>`: Days a flagged role stays withheld (default 30). Default: `30`.

#### `limen review ls`

Reviews. By default those with items for you

```text
Usage: limen review ls [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--all`: Every review (limen:admin or limen:auditor).
- `--json`

#### `limen review items`

The items of a review: yours, or all of them for admins and auditors

```text
Usage: limen review items [OPTIONS] <REVIEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<REVIEW>`

Options:

- `--mine`
- `--open`
- `--json`

#### `limen review certify`

```text
Usage: limen review certify [OPTIONS] <ITEM>
```

Arguments:

- `<ITEM>`

Options:

- `-m, --comment <COMMENT>` Default: ``.

### `limen audit`

Search the audit trail (limen:admin or limen:auditor)

```text
Usage: limen audit [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `limen audit search`

Find audit events and, if the operator indexes them, text from recordings.

Words must all appear. "Quoted phrases" match as written. Filters: user:  resource:  kind:  session:  after:  before:  outcome: Dates are 2026-10-01 or an age such as 24h or 7d. Every search is itself recorded in the audit trail.

```text
Usage: limen audit search [OPTIONS] <QUERY>
```

Arguments:

- `<QUERY>`

Options:

- `--limit <LIMIT>`: The most hits to return (up to 200). Default: `50`.
- `--json`: Output JSON instead of text.

### `limen policy`

Ask a policy questions: test it, who can reach what, what changes

```text
Usage: limen policy [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `limen policy test`

Run the `policy_test` cases in a policy. Exits non-zero if any fails, for CI

```text
Usage: limen policy test [OPTIONS] <PATHS>...
```

Arguments:

- `<PATHS>`: Policy files or directories (roles, mappings, resources, and tests).

Options:

- `--coverage`: Also list the resources and roles that no case touches.
- `--require-cases`: Fail if there are no test cases at all.
- `--json`: Output JSON instead of text.

#### `limen policy who-can`

Who can reach a resource: the roles, groups, bots, and requestable roles

```text
Usage: limen policy who-can [OPTIONS] <RESOURCE>
```

Arguments:

- `<RESOURCE>`

Options:

- `--from <PATH>`: Read the policy from these files or directories (offline).
- `--active`: Ask the running control plane for its active policy (needs limen:admin).
- `--json`

#### `limen policy what-can`

What a group, or a bot, can reach and could ask for

```text
Usage: limen policy what-can [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--group <GROUPS>`: IdP groups. Repeat for a person in several.
- `--bot <BOT>`: A bot instead of groups.
- `--from <PATH>`: Read the policy from these files or directories (offline).
- `--active`: Ask the running control plane for its active policy (needs limen:admin).
- `--json`

#### `limen policy diff`

What changes in who can reach what between two policies, not between two YAML files

```text
Usage: limen policy diff [OPTIONS] --new <NEW> [OLD]...
```

Arguments:

- `<OLD>`: The old policy: files or directories, or `active` for the running one.

Options:

- `--new <NEW>`: The new policy: files or directories (after `--new`).
- `--format <FORMAT>`: text, json, or markdown (for a pull request comment). Values: text, json, markdown. Default: `text`.
- `--fail-on-widening`: Exit non-zero if anyone gains standing access, so CI can ask for a closer look.

Usage: limen redis connect [OPTIONS] <RESOURCE>

### `limen admin`

Administrative commands. These require the limen:admin role

```text
Usage: limen admin [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `limen admin apply`

Validate and apply role, mapping, and resource YAML. Files or directories

```text
Usage: limen admin apply [OPTIONS] <PATHS>...
```

Arguments:

- `<PATHS>`

Options:

- `--dry-run`: Show what would change without applying it.
- `--source-ref <SOURCE_REF>`: Where the policy came from, recorded in the audit trail (for example a Git SHA).
- `--require-tests`: Refuse to apply unless the policy's own `policy_test` cases pass.
- `--source <SOURCE>`: The source these files replace. Documents other sources (and Terraform) manage are left alone; naming one is refused. Default: `default`.

#### `limen admin policy`

Show the active policy version

```text
Usage: limen admin policy [OPTIONS]
```

#### `limen admin token`

Join tokens for proxies and workers

```text
Usage: limen admin token [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

##### `limen admin token create`

Create a single-use join token

```text
Usage: limen admin token create [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--kind <KIND>`: proxy or worker. Default: `worker`.
- `--label <LABELS>`: Labels for the enrolled component, as key=value. Repeatable.
- `--ttl <TTL>`: How long the token stays valid, for example 15m. Default: `15m`.
- `--dns-name <DNS_NAMES>`: DNS names a proxy may put in its certificate. Repeatable.
- `--name <NAME>`: Name the enrolled component may have: exact (given to it even if it asks for none), or a pattern with one `*` matching zero or more of a-z, 0-9 and - (it then picks one with `--name`), such as 'prod-a-*'. Names are for display; the ID stays the identity.

#### `limen admin components`

List enrolled proxies and workers, with their tunnels

```text
Usage: limen admin components [OPTIONS]
```

#### `limen admin lock`

Refuse a user's logins and sessions, and end their open sessions

```text
Usage: limen admin lock [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <USERNAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<USERNAME>`: The user's name, as in the audit trail.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why. Recorded in the audit trail.

#### `limen admin unlock`

Lift a lock. The user can log in again

```text
Usage: limen admin unlock [OPTIONS] <USERNAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<USERNAME>`

#### `limen admin locks`

List locked users

```text
Usage: limen admin locks [OPTIONS]
```

#### `limen admin revoke`

Stop honouring a proxy's or worker's certificate. Its tunnels drop within about 10 seconds

```text
Usage: limen admin revoke [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <COMPONENT_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<COMPONENT_ID>`: The component ID, from `limen admin components`.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why. Recorded in the audit trail.

- `-m, --comment <COMMENT>`

##### `limen admin review overrides`

Roles withheld by a review

```text
Usage: limen admin review overrides [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--all`
- `--json`

##### `limen admin review lift`

Give a withheld role back

```text
Usage: limen admin review lift [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`

#### `limen admin evidence`

A signed pack of compliance evidence for a period

```text
Usage: limen admin evidence [OPTIONS] --from <FROM> --to <TO>
```

Options:

- `--from <FROM>`: First day, as 2026-01-01.
- `--to <TO>`: The day after the last, as 2026-04-01.
- `--out <OUT>` Default: `limen-evidence.json`.

#### `limen admin discovery`

Resources workers found in a cloud account, waiting for you (ADR-0027)

```text
Usage: limen admin discovery [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

##### `limen admin discovery status`

List discovered resources. Pending ones and pending changes come first

```text
Usage: limen admin discovery status [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--state <STATE>`: pending, accepted, rejected, stale, or changed.
- `--json`

##### `limen admin discovery accept`

Make a discovered resource (or its pending change) real

```text
Usage: limen admin discovery accept [OPTIONS] <KEY>
```

Arguments:

- `<KEY>`

Options:

- `--note <NOTE>`

##### `limen admin discovery reject`

Turn a discovered resource away

```text
Usage: limen admin discovery reject [OPTIONS] <KEY>
```

Arguments:

- `<KEY>`

Options:

- `--note <NOTE>`

#### `limen admin grants`

Active access grants, from approved requests and break-glass

```text
Usage: limen admin grants [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--all`: Also grants that ended in the last 30 days.
- `--json`

#### `limen admin revoke-grant`

End an access grant, and the sessions it allowed

```text
Usage: limen admin revoke-grant [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <REQUEST_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<REQUEST_ID>`: The request id, from `limen admin grants`.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why. Recorded in the audit trail.

#### `limen admin kill-session`

End one live session

```text
Usage: limen admin kill-session [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <SESSION_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<SESSION_ID>`: The session ID, from `session.start` in the audit trail.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why. Recorded in the audit trail.

### `limen manage`

The management API: read policy documents and write resources, as an admin or as a bot with a policy_writer grant (ADR-0042)

```text
Usage: limen manage [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

#### `limen manage whoami`

What you may read and write: admin, or your writer grant

```text
Usage: limen manage whoami [OPTIONS]
```

#### `limen manage ls`

List documents of one kind (resource, role, resource_profile, ...)

```text
Usage: limen manage ls [OPTIONS] <KIND>
```

Arguments:

- `<KIND>`

Options:

- `--namespace <NAMESPACE>`: Only this namespace (a writer's own is implied).
- `--source <SOURCE>`: Only documents this source manages.

#### `limen manage get`

Show one document, with its owner and etag

```text
Usage: limen manage get [OPTIONS] <KIND> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<KIND>`
- `<NAME>`

#### `limen manage put-resource`

Create a resource, or with --etag replace it. A writer completes a profile: --spec holds only the fields the profile lets it set

```text
Usage: limen manage put-resource [OPTIONS] --spec <SPEC> --source <SOURCE> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`

Options:

- `--profile <PROFILE>`: The profile it completes. Required for bot writers.
- `--spec <SPEC>`: The resource spec as JSON, for example '{"postgres":{"endpoint":"db.internal:5432"}}'.
- `--label <LABELS>`: key=value. Repeatable.
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--source <SOURCE>`: Who you write as, such as terraform/payments-prod.
- `--namespace <NAMESPACE>`: Defaults to a writer's namespace, or `default` for admins.
- `--etag <ETAG>`: Replace the resource with this etag (from `limen manage get`).
- `--dry-run`: Check everything and show the impact, but change nothing.
- `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>`: Makes a retry safe: the same id returns the first result.

#### `limen manage delete-resource`

Delete a resource you manage

```text
Usage: limen manage delete-resource [OPTIONS] --source <SOURCE> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`

Options:

- `--source <SOURCE>`
- `--namespace <NAMESPACE>`
- `--etag <ETAG>`: Required unless --if-exists.
- `--if-exists`: Succeed when it's already gone.
